clue.text: "Penny, Leonard, I'm working with: NASA, Dr A Noel … and DNA Leonard!" as an example

definitions.text: NASA, Dr A Noel … and DNA Leonard!" as an example

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for a penny in British money

indicators.note: working means the letters of the two words are set in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: Penny lists the people she works with, ending in a strange string of names that includes Leonard twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'NASA, Dr A Noel … and DNA Leonard' reads the same backwards and forwards once spaces and punctuation are ignored, so it is offered as an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase that reads identically in either direction is the standard example of this kind of wordplay.

clue.text: One turns elements into sub-atomic particles

indicators.note: breaking the words into their elements and rebuilding them signals a rearrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A physics statement about something that changes chemical elements into smaller particles.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests transmutation of elements; in fact 'elements into' tells you to break 'One turns' into its letters and rebuild them.
explanation.definitionFit: These uncharged particles sit with protons in an atomic nucleus, so they are sub-atomic.

clue.text: Bit of a laugh with first half of series on cable

parts.note: ha is a single burst of laughter

indicators.note: first half of means keep only the opening three of the six letters of series

explanation.surface: A little comedy alongside the start of a series broadcast on cable television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cable' looks like cable TV, the channel the series is on; here it means a thick rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A hawser is a heavy rope or cable used for mooring or towing a ship.

clue.text: What you might pick as odd bits of social behaviour initially

indicators.note: odd bits means the first, third and fifth letters of the word social
initially means take only the opening letter of behaviour

explanation.surface: Picking out the strange elements of how someone acts in company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pick' suggests choosing; the definition means the crust on a healing wound that people pick at.
explanation.definitionFit: A dried crust over a wound is the thing people are tempted to pick at.

clue.text: Howard is disheartened, imbibing ale and getting drunk to make a point

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so the outer letters take the other letters inside them
disheartened means the word Howard loses its middle, leaving only its outer letters
getting drunk means the letters of ale and and are reeled around into a new order

explanation.surface: Howard, feeling low, downs some ale and gets drunk to prove something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point' seems to be an argument to make; it is a promontory. 'Disheartened' leaves HD, which takes in EADLAN, the rearrangement of ALE AND.
explanation.definitionFit: A headland is a point of land jutting into the sea, as in a coastal point.

clue.text: Hey! It's not really a Big Bang Theory's second parts that might interest Professor Green

parts.note: hi is a greeting like hey

indicators.note: parts means the small bang word is split open so the picked letter can go inside it

parts.note: a pop is a small bang, nothing like a big one

indicators.note: second means take the second letter of the word Theory's

explanation.surface: A cry about the Big Bang Theory TV show and something to catch a professor's interest.
explanation.walkthrough: Professor Green is a British rapper, not an academic like the show's characters; the definition is the music he makes.
explanation.definitionFit: Professor Green is a British rapper, so this rap-based music genre is what interests him.

clue.text: Degree covering energy and Newton's studies

indicators.note: in a down answer the first piece covers, or sits on top of, the rest
and simply joins the energy letter to the Newton letters that follow it

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
N is the symbol for the newton, the unit of force, and the possessive adds S

explanation.surface: A degree course in energy and the work of Isaac Newton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Studies' looks like academic work; here it means private rooms for working.
explanation.definitionFit: A den is a small private room where someone reads or works, much like a study.

clue.text: Hot girl is to live next door to bachelor

indicators.note: next door to means the living word sits immediately alongside the bachelor one

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts
to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: An attractive woman moves in next to a single man, as Penny does in the show.
explanation.definitionFit: Babe is slang for a sexy, attractive young woman.

clue.text: Bill, named in show's titles, gets recognised …

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill
to be credited is to be named in a programme's credits

explanation.surface: Someone called Bill appears in a show's credits and so gets recognition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a person's name; it is an account, abbreviated AC.
explanation.definitionFit: Accredited means officially recognised or approved.

clue.text: … at university, during his break

indicators.note: during means the university words sit within the word his

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: while at university he takes some time off.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiatus is a pause or gap in proceedings.

clue.text: He follows Indian teaching his friend & Penny to go ahead getting to 3rd in date

indicators.note: to go ahead means the friend and penny come in front of his

parts.note: a bud is a buddy or friend
D, from the Latin denarius, was the old British penny

indicators.note: 3rd in means the third letter of the word date

explanation.surface: A man teaching his friend and Penny, with a date coming up.
explanation.walkthrough: D for penny comes from the pre-1971 British currency of pounds, shillings and pence.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of the Buddha's teaching, which arose in India, belongs to this religion.

clue.text: Sound Raj can make stops temporarily

indicators.note: can make means the letters of the two words can be made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Raj from the show is able to make a noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like a noise or a homophone signal; it is just part of the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A meeting that adjourns breaks off for a while, intending to resume later.

clue.text: It has been given National Television Award by Monica and Barbara in California?

definitions.text: by Monica and Barbara in California?

parts.note: it, in old slang, is sex appeal, abbreviated SA
NTA is the abbreviation for a National Television Award

explanation.surface: Something given a TV award along with two actresses in California.
explanation.walkthrough: Santa Monica and Santa Barbara are Californian cities, so the answer comes before, or 'by', those names there; the question mark flags the indirect definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The word pairs with Monica and Barbara to name two Californian cities, Santa Monica and Santa Barbara.

clue.text: Couple from Pasadena, California, follow almost all this material

indicators.note: follow means the Pasadena and California letters come after the shortened all
almost means the last letter of the word all is cut
couple from means the first two letters of Pasadena

parts.note: CA is the postal abbreviation for California

explanation.surface: A pair of people from Pasadena, where the show is set, adopt nearly everything about some fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpaca is a soft wool cloth made from the fleece of the South American animal.

clue.text: Doctor S Cooper: "I'm accepting money for accommodation"

indicators.note: accepting means the rearranged letters take the money letter inside them
doctor as a verb means to tamper with, so these letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Dr Sheldon Cooper announces that he will take payment for letting out a room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor S Cooper' looks like Sheldon's title, but 'Doctor' is the anagram signal, making COMPROISE, which 'accepting' opens to take M. 'Accommodation' means coming to terms, not lodging.
explanation.definitionFit: Reaching an accommodation means settling a dispute by each side conceding something.

clue.text: Fellows at university have to act, with new series …

parts.note: to do is to act or perform
S is an abbreviation for series

explanation.surface: University fellows have to perform in a new run of a TV show.
explanation.definitionFit: At Oxford and Cambridge, dons are the fellows and tutors of a college.

clue.text: … made perfect by broadcasting the finale in high definition

indicators.note: in means these letters go inside the high-definition letters

parts.note: a programme that is on is being broadcast

indicators.note: finale means the closing letter of the word the

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: the series ending is polished by being shown in high definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To hone something is to sharpen or refine it until it is just right.

clue.text: Part Sheldon took and kept

indicators.note: part means only a portion of the letters running through Sheldon took is used

explanation.surface: Sheldon accepted an acting role and stayed in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part' looks like an acting role Sheldon took; it signals a run of letters inside the words.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal-verb synonym: retaining something firmly in your grasp is keeping it.

clue.text: Head of department at uni meeting doctor is lost for words

indicators.note: head of means the opening letter of department

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for university
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A university department head meets a doctor and is left speechless.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dumb means being unable or unwilling to speak, so speechless.

clue.text: Ditching loose woman, Howard has this problem (figuratively)

parts.words: Ditching loose woman, Howard has this
parts.note: Howard without HO, slang for a loose woman, is WARD, which this answer spells when its first part is written backwards, as its second part says

explanation.surface: Howard Wolowitz, having dumped a woman, now has a difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figuratively' warns that the answer is to be read as an instruction: its first half turned back gives what remains of Howard once the loose woman goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawback is a disadvantage or snag, a synonym for a problem.

clue.text: Tequila, for example, found in academe's Caltech

indicators.note: found in means the letters sit inside the words academe's Caltech

explanation.surface: Tequila turning up among the academics at Caltech, where the show's scientists work.
explanation.definitionFit: Mescal is any Mexican spirit distilled from agave, and tequila is one specific kind.

clue.text: Co-worker knocked his heart out for "Penny! Penny! Penny!" for example

indicators.note: knocked his heart out for means the central letters of the co-worker word are removed and replaced

parts.note: taken as written, without the hyphen
P is the abbreviation for a penny, twice over

explanation.surface: A colleague knocks on a door calling a name three times, as Sheldon does at Penny's door.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of COWORKER is WORK; swapping it for PP leaves the answer, and the last 'Penny' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: British pennies are bronze coins long called coppers, so a penny is an example of one.

clue.text: Physicist is one that's taken against convert or God about origin of atoms

parts.note: A means one, as in a single thing
V is short for versus, against

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the next letter
convert means the letters of or and God are changed into a new arrangement
origin of means the opening letter of atoms

explanation.surface: A physicist taking a stand against religious conversion and the idea that God made atoms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Convert' looks like a religious convert but signals the rearrangement OGDRO; 'about' wraps that round the A from atoms.
explanation.definitionFit: Amedeo Avogadro was the Italian physicist behind Avogadro's law and the number of particles in a mole.

clue.text: Lectured from reference book about lab animal …

indicators.note: about means the dictionary letters go round the animal

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
the rat is the classic laboratory animal

explanation.surface: Someone gave a talk using a reference book about a laboratory rat.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to deliver a formal speech, so lectured fits the past tense.

clue.text: I park on the street behind Sheldon: Leonard heads for exit

indicators.note: behind means the I park street pieces come after the two initials
heads means the first letters of Sheldon and Leonard

parts.note: P is the map and road-sign abbreviation for parking
a road is a street

explanation.surface: Someone parks on the street behind Sheldon while Leonard leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: A slip road is the British term for a short road used to leave or join a motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip road is the short road by which drivers leave a motorway, so it serves as an exit.

clue.text: … to get help with line on set

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece placed on another sits above it

parts.note: aid is help

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: getting assistance with lines on a film set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' looks like a film set; it is the past tense of set, meaning put down.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid and set are both past forms meaning put down in place.

clue.text: Doctor Amy nearly got shot

indicators.note: nearly means the name Amy loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Dr Amy Farrah Fowler from the show was almost hit by a bullet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' looks like gunfire; it is a small measure of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A dram is a small drink of spirits, the same as a shot.

clue.text: Bernadette's beginning to go through US graduate's records

indicators.note: to go through means that letter passes into the graduates word

parts.note: alums is American slang for alumni, graduates

indicators.note: beginning means the first letter of Bernadette's

explanation.surface: Bernadette starts searching an American graduate's files.
explanation.definitionFit: Albums are collections of recorded music, so records in the LP sense.

clue.text: I've a degree from Californian city that invested $0.01 I note

indicators.note: invested means the city letters are wrapped round the money and the two I letters

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
the I of I've is used; the 've, short for have, says the city has it
one hundredth of a dollar is a cent
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A graduate of a Californian university that put a cent into something boasts of a qualification.
explanation.definitionFit: A licentiate is a qualification below a doctorate awarded by some universities, especially in Europe.

clue.text: In the beginning Chuck has a way to get actors

indicators.note: in the beginning means take the first letter of Chuck

parts.note: ST, short for street, is a way

explanation.surface: Chuck Lorre, the show's creator, finds a way to get his actors at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A cast is the full company of actors in a production.
